title: Ask the service
briefing: The status service at status.internal exposes a health endpoint. Ops wants
its current build token recorded for the deploy log.
Fetch http://status.internal/health and capture the reply.
tips: `curl URL` fetches a page and prints the body. Redirect it to a file with >.
The reply contains a line like token=XXimage. You need the whole reply saved.
objective: Fetch http://status.internal/health and save the response body to ~/health.txt.
hints: First check the name resolves: `dig +short status.internal` (or just curl it).
`curl -s http://status.internal/health > ~/health.txt` — then `cat ~/health.txt` to see the token.
explanation: `curl` is how you talk to a web service from the shell — health checks, APIs, debugging a proxy. The body prints to stdout, so a redirect (`> file`) or a pipe (`| grep`) captures exactly what the server said.
